title: 4 Surprising Ways EQ Can Make or Break Your Ambitions
author: Colette Molteni
summary: Colette Molteni argues that emotional intelligence, more than IQ, determines whether professionals achieve their goals, and she walks through the four EQ domains with a personal or observed story for each. Self-awareness is illustrated by rescheduling workouts around her energy crash. Self-management is shown through a two-week sprint to get an Agile certification. Social awareness is shown by a friend who asked for a raise just after the company downsized its space and was soon let go. Relationship management is shown by a LinkedIn contact who ignored two referrals and lost her goodwill. She closes by claiming empathy drives all four pillars. The stories are anecdotal and the 80 percent EQ statistic is a secondhand figure, but the practical takeaways for professional behaviour are clear.
points: Self-awareness means designing goals around your actual energy and constraints rather than around willpower.
Self-management means arranging conditions, such as time blocks and closed calendars, that work when nobody is watching.
Social awareness means timing requests to the context, such as the organization's cost-cutting mood, before asking for a raise.
Relationship management includes acknowledging help; people who offer referrals and get silence stop offering.
Empathy underlies the four pillars and does not require absorbing other people's emotions, only relating to how they might feel.
quotes: Sit, think, and plan your goals according to what your body needs. This applies not just to exercise but also to diet plans and project goals. Be self-aware and listen inward.
Achieving your goals and aspirations takes self-management and strategizing how you will get it done. Feeling hopeful or motivated is not enough.
His boss had just shut down some of the office space and sublet it out to save money. The boss was in a mindset to save money, not spend it. My friend did not read the room.
The takeaway here is not that you will get fired by asking for a raise at the wrong time. The lesson is to read the room and use social awareness strategically with your goals.
Your network is your net worth when you need a new job, a referral, or even potential new clients. Business is built on relationships, not simply products and services. Manage your relationships.

Remember, empathy is not about being a puddle of mush. You do not even have to bring yourself down into their emotions; you can simply relate to a time you felt similarly or think of how they must feel.
